What comes up in Tuggerah

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. Treat the rows as the usual shape of the job locally. A specific property can differ, and that is what a site visit settles.

Warehouse with slab and hardstand

On an industrial site there is frequently more concrete than building.

How it is handled
Structure removed first, then the slab and hardstand broken out and crushed so the clean concrete is reused.
What does it
Large excavator with a shear or grapple, hydraulic hammer, truck and dogs.

Retail tenancy strip out

Fit out, linings and services out of a building that stays standing.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, structural elements identified, then removal by hand with the neighbouring tenancies kept open.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant, material loaded at the service area.

Internal strip outs and partial removal

Walls, floors, linings and fit out taken out of a building that stays standing, usually ahead of a renovation rather than a rebuild.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, then the removal done by hand so that what remains is not disturbed. Structural elements are identified before anything is cut.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant only, with material carried out and loaded at the kerb.

Tuggerah

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Commercial and industrial land Warehouse, retail and light industrial work rather than knockdowns.
  • Good heavy vehicle access Built for it, which helps the cartage considerably.
  • Slabs and hardstand Frequently a larger part of the job than the building is.
  • Operating neighbours Tenancies that keep trading through the work, so hoarding and hours are planned around them.

Tuggerah is set up for trucks, so cartage is rarely the constraint and a truck and dog can usually stand and load properly. The planning effort goes into working alongside businesses that stay open rather than into plant access.

Tuggerah questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish warehouses and retail premises?
Yes. It is licensed work and it runs as a sequence: hazardous materials survey, service disconnections, soft strip, then the structure, with steel and clean concrete separated as it comes down.
What happens to the concrete?
Clean concrete is crushed and reused rather than landfilled, which is usually the cheaper outcome as well as the better one. Keeping it apart from mixed waste is what makes that possible.
The street is narrow and the block is steep. What can get in?
Smaller plant working for longer, with spoil taken out as it is generated. On the beachside streets a truck and dog frequently is not an option, so the same volume goes out in more tipper loads.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
